subject: English
title: Text Response Unit — Y7 English
tool_context: Analytical text response unit — students read a literary or multimodal text, analyse how language and literary devices create meaning, and produce a written analytical response. The unit activates Literature examining and responding strands alongside Literacy analysing and creating strands. Language concept standards (evaluative language, sentence structure) are activated as tools for writing.
progression_endpoint: Students produce a written analytical response to a literary or multimodal text that explains how specific literary devices and language features create meaning, supports evaluative claims with textual evidence, and uses complex sentence structures and evaluative vocabulary deliberately to convey a reasoned interpretation.

phases.label: Reading
phases.checkpoint: Students can identify the significant ideas, issues and context of the text and explain how characters, settings and events combine to create meaning — they are ready to move from plot-level reading to analytical reading.

waypoints.note: First encounter with the text — establish the historical, social or cultural context before analytical reading begins.
Inferencing while reading — students practise reading beyond the literal as they encounter the text for the first time.
Explore how ideas are represented differently across contexts — activates when text is compared to other works or student prior reading.

phases.label: Analysing
phases.checkpoint: Students can explain how specific literary devices and language features create character, influence emotions and opinions, and create layers of meaning in the text — they have the analytical content needed to write a response.

waypoints.note: Identifying idea structures (cause-effect, extended metaphor) in the text — activates during close analytical reading, before writing begins.
Summarising key ideas and arguments in the text — prepares students to make focused analytical claims rather than broad plot summaries.
Building evaluative vocabulary as an analytical tool — introduced here so students have the language to name what they are noticing in the text.

phases.label: Drafting
phases.checkpoint: Students can produce a draft analytical response that makes at least two evaluative claims about the text, substantiates each with textual evidence, and uses complex sentence structures to elaborate and explain their reasoning.

waypoints.note: Forming and justifying a personal opinion about the text — the opinion-forming step that precedes writing the response.
Substantiating evaluations with textual reference — the core move of the analytical response.
Using complex and compound-complex sentences to elaborate, extend and explain analytical claims — sentence structure as a writing tool in the response.
Planning the response — purpose (analytical), audience, and structural choices before drafting begins.
Using idea structures (cause-effect, extended metaphor explanation) in the response — organising analytical claims with appropriate idea structures.

phases.label: Publishing
phases.checkpoint: Students can produce a published analytical response that forms and justifies a reasoned interpretation of the text, uses appropriate metalanguage, and demonstrates deliberate language and structural choices — the response shows the integrated analytical and writing capabilities developed across the unit.

waypoints.note: Engaging with others' opinions — peer review of draft responses before final publication; students identify where their interpretation agrees or differs with peers.
Sentence structure as deliberate choice in the final response — editing for variation and effect, not just correctness.
Final check that language feature analysis in the response is connected to audience and purpose — does the analytical claim explain how the feature shapes meaning for a reader?
